content_html:
Cusco is a city full of history, culture and tradition. In addition to its impressive archaeological sites, it is also home to museums that offer a unique look at the Inca, colonial and contemporary past. If you visit the historic capital of Peru, these are the museums you cannot miss.

1. Inka Museum

  • Location: Cuesta del Almirante 103, Cusco
  • Schedule: Monday to Saturday, from 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m.
  • Entry: Approximately S/ 10

The Inka Museum is the ideal place to understand the history of the Incas. Here you will find an incredible collection of well-preserved Inca ceramics, textiles, tools, weapons and mummies. The most impressive thing are the quipus, ancient knot systems used to record information.

Don't miss: The recreation of an Inca tomb with mummies and funerary offerings.

2. Museum of Pre-Columbian Art (MAP)

  • Location: Plaza de las Nazarenas 231, Cusco
  • Schedule: Every day, from 9:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. to 10:00 p.m.
  • Entry: S/ 20 approx.

This museum presents an impressive collection of pre-Columbian pieces from various cultures of Peru, including the Mochica, Nazca and Chavín. It is located in a colonial house from the 16th century, which gives it a special atmosphere.

Don't miss: The gold room and sculptural ceramics of the Mochica culture.

3. Qorikancha Site Museum

  • Location: Av. El Sol, next to the Santo Domingo Convent
  • Schedule: Monday to Saturday, from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.
  • Entry: Included in the Cusco Tourist Ticket

The Qorikancha was the most sacred temple of the Incas, covered in gold before the arrival of the Spanish. The museum, located at its base, displays Inca artifacts, metal tools, mummies and ceremonial objects found in excavations.

Don't miss: The remains of original Inca walls, which show the perfection in Inca engineering.

4. Regional Historical Museum of Cusco (Casa Garcilaso)

  • Location: Calle Heladeros 165, Cusco
  • Schedule: Monday to Sunday, from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.
  • Entry: Included in the Tourist Ticket

This museum is in the birthplace of Inca Garcilaso de la Vega, the first mestizo chronicler of Peruvian history. Here you will learn about the history of Cusco from pre-Inca times to the arrival of the Spanish.

Don't miss: Garcilaso's personal objects and the colonial paintings of the Cusco School.

5. Coca Museum

  • Location: 122 Palacio Street, Cusco
  • Schedule: Every day, from 9:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. to 7:00 p.m.
  • Entry: S/ 10 approx.

The coca leaf has been a sacred symbol in the Andes for centuries. This museum explores its use in Inca culture and its importance in the current life of the Andean people. It also shows its history in the modern industry.

Don't miss: The explanation of the ritual use of coca in Andean ceremonies.
